answer: A farm must therefore either lie, which the meadow graph proves on replay, or recruit 120 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the inlet registry records each claim and the jetty audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 68% of the attester's bond. That is 11 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
